title: Break constraints import-cycle SCC: extract ConstraintFinding/FindingDelta to a leaf module
description:
sutra's own builtin:cycles blocking violation covers the SCC {waivers.rs, tools/review.rs, constraints/check.rs} (pre-existing), and bafae79 added constraints/external.rs into it via mutual import: check.rs uses external, external.rs uses check::{ConstraintFinding, FindingDelta}.

ConstraintFinding and FindingDelta are pure data types consumed by waivers, review, check, and external. Moving them to a leaf module (e.g. constraints/mod.rs or a new constraints/finding.rs) with re-exports breaks both the new check↔external 2-cycle and the pre-existing waivers→check edge of the SCC (waivers.rs:3 imports check only for ConstraintFinding). waivers.rs:5 also imports review::ConventionViolation — check whether that type should move too to fully dissolve the SCC.

Found by vidhi-review of sutra/needs-designing/14.
execution_record: Went as planned. One minor surprise: check.rs needed `pub use` re-exports of the moved types so that downstream consumers using `check::ConstraintFinding` paths (tools/constraints.rs) continued to compile. Also review.rs's import needed `pub use` for the test crate.

messages.author: codex
messages.text: Codex adversarial review: **approve**. No ship-blocking issues found. The old waivers↔review and check↔external edges are removed, compatibility re-exports preserve checked public paths, and FcaEngine::check() already returns conventions::ConventionViolation. No material findings. (Codex could not run cargo check in its sandbox — already verified locally: all 374 unit tests + 30 integration suites pass.)
